title: Hybridisation
examples: What is the difference between sigma and pi bonds?
How does the number of bonds determine the type of hybridisation?
Can you show me the hybridisation for methane?

explain.say: Today we learn about hybridisation in bonding.

items: These new orbitals are used for bonding.

explain.say: When a carbon atom has four single bonds, it uses sp3 hybridisation.
If carbon forms a double bond, it uses sp2 hybridisation.
For three double bonds, carbon uses sp hybridisation.
Sigma bonds are formed by direct head-on overlap of orbitals.
Pi bonds are formed by the side-by-side overlap of unhybridised p orbitals.

faq.q: What is the difference between sigma and pi bonds?
faq.a: Sigma bonds are formed by the direct overlap of orbitals end-to-end. Pi bonds are formed by the side-by-side overlap of unhybridised p orbitals.
asks: How do sigma and pi bonds form?
Can you explain the difference in overlap?

faq.q: Why does hybridization change based on the number of bonds?
faq.a: The number of electron domains determines how many orbitals must mix. This mixing results in specific geometries like tetrahedral or trigonal planar.
asks: Does the geometry dictate the hybridization?

faq.q: Does every bond have a sigma component?
faq.a: Yes, every single bond, whether it is a single, double, or triple bond, always contains one sigma bond. The extra bonds are pi bonds.
asks: Is a double bond just one sigma and one pi?
What is the minimum number of sigma bonds?

faq.q: What is the relationship between hybridization and molecular shape?
faq.a: The hybridization predicts the geometry around the central atom. For example, sp3 hybridization leads to a tetrahedral shape.
asks: Can you relate sp2 to geometry?

faq.q: If I see an ethene molecule, what hybridization should I expect?
faq.a: Ethene has a carbon with one double bond, which requires sp2 hybridization. This gives it a trigonal planar geometry.
asks: What is the hybridization for C=C?
How do I find the hybridization for ethene?

facts: sp3 hybridization results in a tetrahedral geometry with bond angles near one hundred ten degrees.
sp2 hybridization results in a trigonal planar geometry with bond angles of one hundred twenty degrees.
A double bond consists of one sigma bond and one pi bond.
Pi bonds are formed using the remaining unhybridised p orbitals.

quiz.say: A central atom forming four single bonds will exhibit which hybridization?
quiz.why: Four single bonds require four equivalent orbitals, which results in sp3 hybridization and a tetrahedral shape.

wrong.0: This is not a valid hybridization state; hybridization always involves mixing of s and p orbitals.
wrong.2: This is wrong because sp hybridization is used when there are only two electron domains, like in a linear molecule.
wrong.3: This is wrong because sp2 is used for three electron domains, like in a trigonal planar arrangement.

quiz.say: Which type of bond overlap creates the pi bond?

options.show: Overlap between s and p orbitals
options.say: Overlap between s and p orbitals

quiz.why: Pi bonds are specifically formed by the lateral overlap of unhybridised p orbitals, not head-on overlap.

wrong.1: Head-on overlap describes the formation of the stronger sigma bond.
wrong.2: This mixing process is what creates the new hybrid orbitals, not the pi bond itself.
wrong.3: While d orbitals can be involved in advanced bonding, pi bonds primarily use unhybridised p orbitals.

quiz.say: If a carbon atom has one double bond and two single bonds, its hybridization is:
quiz.why: The total number of electron domains is three (one from the double bond, two from the single bonds), which dictates sp2 hybridization.

wrong.1: sp3 is used for four electron domains, which is more than the three domains present here.
wrong.2: sp is used for only two electron domains, which is fewer than the three domains present here.
wrong.3: sp3d is used when there are five electron domains, which is more than the three domains present here.
